heading: PPF for NRIs: Continuing Your Account After Moving Abroad
tldr: Existing Public Provident Fund (PPF) accounts can be continued by Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) until their original maturity period.
NRIs are not permitted to make new contributions to their PPF accounts after acquiring NRI status.
The interest earned on PPF accounts held by NRIs continues to be tax-exempt under Indian income tax laws.
At maturity, NRIs can either withdraw the balance or extend the account without making further contributions.
If an Indian citizen acquires foreign citizenship, their PPF account must be closed immediately.
caption:
Moving abroad doesn't always mean saying goodbye to your PPF! If you're an NRI, you can keep your existing account until it matures, and the interest stays tax-free. However, you can't add new money. If you become a foreign citizen, though, you'll need to close it. Understand these simple rules for your PPF. Read more in the article.
